square.notes: No frame from 2019 or later shows the square's interior: the only later frames (2020) are on Wellington Street beside City Hall, looking along the street. They show a wide pale concrete sidewalk along the City Hall side of the square with a granite-grey curb, tall black lamp posts, young street trees, and the two- and three-storey red and buff brick fronts opposite. The square's paving, seating and planting could not be described from 2019+ photos; the 2017 frames (pale concrete panels, charcoal paver bands, black bollards, concrete block seats) were taken just after the rebuild, some with construction hoarding, and are not used here.

city-hall.notes: Deep red brick throughout over a tall rock-faced grey limestone basement that reads as about one full storey (taller than the 2.2 m plinth in the current model, roughly 3-3.5 m on the Wellington Street side). The ends of the building are full-height rounded/polygonal bays (three storeys of brick) capped by conical slate roofs with finials, not small turrets standing at the corners. Main front: a wide flight of steps rising to a round-arched entrance under a balcony, rows of stepped/shaped gables and dormers with white-painted copings and finials, white window trim. The clock tower rises from the middle of the front with a tall dark slate spire, small corner pinnacles and a flagpole. Roofs dark grey slate. Frames on Wellington Street show hanging baskets and black lamp posts along the sidewalk, red-and-white bunting under the windows on event days.

courthouse.notes: Buff (cream-yellow) brick confirmed, with dark red-brown sandstone bands, window surrounds and cornice; round-arched windows in pairs; tower at the front corner with a tall, steep dark spire and a pointed finial; front gable with a row of arched windows; set back behind lawn, large spruces and deciduous trees that hide much of it in summer. The model's buff walls and corner tower match; the photos show more red-brown banding and darker trim than plain buff.

avon-theatre.notes: The Downie Street front is a three-storey cream stone-slab facade with deep-set windows, a row of small roofline brackets and a green-tinted glass-and-metal marquee canopy with stairs and steel rails each side; the current model only adds a marquee box and a blade sign to a generic front. Along George Street the building is red brick (Studio Theatre) with glass-block windows on a concrete base and a round oculus; behind rises a tall plain stage house in grey/beige render with exterior fire escapes and a black-clad fly tower carrying a large poster frame.

market-square.notes: See 'square': no 2019+ frame shows the square itself. The 2020 frames along Wellington Street show the City Hall side edge (pale concrete sidewalk, black lamp posts, young trees) and the continuous two- and three-storey brick fronts facing it.
